source: Native AWS CLI captures, projected without a local evaluation oracle. Case expected/prior_state objects are copied from parsed HistoryData newState/oldState; the retention contrast is copied from DescribeAlarms. Source indices and JSON pointers are zero-based.

limitations: Metric points cannot be deleted; account-owned alarms will be deleted in finally.
Observed evaluation ranges are specific to these configurations; no universal N+2 inference.
Only single-metric static-threshold sliding-window alarms; no external actions or namespace special cases.

Initial baseline interrupted by shared Python-kernel function-name collision. No metric data had been published; all eight owned alarms were deleted successfully. Experiment resumed in an isolated namespace; raw requests from both attempts retained.

Following the initial kernel interruption, later deliberate windows were bounded at 150/120/150/110 seconds to keep combined attempts within 20 minutes plus cleanup; individual reasonData/histories establish visibility, not a universal timing guarantee.

Initial isolated-breach publication did not include an independent metric retrieval: its first few seconds of missing snapshots cannot alone distinguish ingestion lag from evaluation delay; simultaneous M2/M3 contrast and later histories establish the observed difference.

DescribeAlarms StateReasonData may remain unchanged while alarm state is unchanged. History records transitions/configuration, not every internal evaluation; inferred lookback slot counts are bounded observations, not a documented exact retrieval algorithm.
Period60 control retained older history across phases; it establishes aggregation and observed transitions but does not isolate a complete no-data expiration range.
Raw CLI timestamp offsets (+01:00) and UTC StateReasonData strings are preserved as received for later normalization.

cleanup.dependencyOrder: No alarm-to-alarm dependencies; delete owned query and both scalar alarms together after capturing history.

undeletableMetricFootprint.reason: CloudWatch custom metric samples have no delete API; samples age out under CloudWatch retention. No ongoing publisher remains.

documentation.text: For percentiles between 0.5 (inclusive) and 1.00 (exclusive), low-sample setting is used with fewer than 10/(1-percentile) data points during evaluation period. p90 nominal boundary 100 samples.
documentation.fullBoundaryText: For percentiles between 0.5 (inclusive) and 1.00 (exclusive), this setting is used when there are fewer than 10/(1-percentile) data points during the evaluation period. For example, this setting would be used if there were fewer than 1000 samples for an alarm on a p99 percentile. For percentiles between 0 and 0.5 (exclusive), the setting is used when there are fewer than 10/percentile data points.

query-admission.note: Independent empty-data transitions; no metric publication. Full call history and bounded timing limitations are retained in the source fixture.

replay_notes: Each case is independent. Create one evaluation cadence before captured StateReasonData.queryDate, publish every successful native PutMetricData completed before that queryDate (including old publications), seed captured oldState when noninitial, advance to queryDate and drain production jobs through the SDK-created alarm.

Publications are replayed synchronously at setup time with their original sample timestamps. Their original request start/finish times are provenance and determine inclusion, not an ingestion-lag simulator.

Compare state and structured reason data, including actual recent/evaluated values, null gaps, counts, timestamps and presence/absence of scalar statistic/unit/sampleCount fields. Ignore StateReason prose and AWS processing/state-update latency.
queryDate is the evaluation instant, never the later DescribeAlarms or DescribeAlarmHistory request time. Retained unchanged state does not expose every native evaluation.
Expression and scalar evidence have different query phases; retain exact native queryDates rather than shifting them to fit one local window.
No universal N+2 lookback or AWS latency guarantee is inferred from these bounded configurations.

evidence_only.name: isolated-breach-early-missing-snapshot
evidence_only.limitation: The first DescribeAlarms after successful isolated-breach publication still exposes older missing-state reason data. No independent retrieval established immediate ingestion, and unchanged state does not expose the current evaluator queryDate. This snapshot cannot be replayed as a new evaluation at Describe request time without inventing ingestion lag or evaluation timing; retained here, not asserted as a deterministic empty window. Later actual transition queryDates are exercised by isolated-premature-m2/m3 and isolated-breach-expires.
